ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(xvla): compute select_action chunks through predict_action_chunk …
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(xvla): compute select_action chunks through predict_action_chunk (#4827)

* fix(xvla): compute select_action chunks through predict_action_chunk

lerobot-rollout --use_torch_compile compiles a policy by wrapping its
predict_action_chunk with torch.compile. X-VLA's select_action called the
internal _get_action_chunk instead, so the compiled wrapper never ran and
X-VLA stayed uncompiled, while the rollout still logged that compilation
was configured. X-VLA has no compile setting of its own, so this wrapper
is the only way the flag can reach it.

Compute each new chunk through predict_action_chunk, as most chunking
policies already do, and pass the noise argument on to it.
predict_action_chunk calls the same _get_action_chunk. Its observation
queue update now runs only on the ticks that compute a chunk, which
changes nothing for X-VLA because its only queue holds actions.

The new test keeps the real predict_action_chunk and records each call to
it, the same way the rollout installs its wrapper, and replaces only the
chunk computation inside it with a fresh random chunk per call. It checks
that select_action computes exactly two chunks through predict_action_chunk,
passes the same batch and noise each time, and returns the first
n_action_steps actions of the first chunk and then the first action of the
next one. It fails without the change.

* test(xvla): drop select_action routing test

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(policies): accept the starting noise in predict_action_chunk for…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(policies): accept the starting noise in predict_action_chunk for EO-1, EVO-1, WALL-OSS and Wall-OSS-0.5 (#4811)

* feat(eo1): accept noise in predict_action_chunk

EO-1 always drew its own starting noise inside sample_actions, so a caller
could not pass it in. predict_action_chunk and select_action now take a
keyword-only noise argument. select_action passes it to
predict_action_chunk, which forwards it to sample_actions. When it is None,
the noise is drawn exactly as before. A given noise is moved to the device
and dtype of the draw it replaces, and the denoising loop does not write
into it, so the caller's tensor is not changed.

predict_action_chunk no longer ends in a **kwargs that nothing read, so a
misspelled keyword such as noize= raises a TypeError instead of silently
falling back to a fresh draw.

* feat(evo1): accept noise in predict_action_chunk

EVO-1 always drew its own starting sample inside the flow matching head, so
a caller could not pass it in. predict_action_chunk and select_action now
take a keyword-only noise argument. select_action passes it to
predict_action_chunk, which forwards it through Evo1Model to
FlowmatchingActionHead.get_action. When it is None, the sample is drawn
exactly as before. A given noise is moved to the device and dtype of the
draw it replaces, and the loop does not write into it, so the caller's
tensor is not changed.

The noise is shaped (batch_size, chunk_size, max_action_dim), like the
actions EVO-1 returns and the noise of the other policies. A tensor of
another shape raises a ValueError, so a noise laid out differently with the
same number of values is not silently read in the wrong order.

select_action used to accept any keyword and drop it. It now takes only
noise, so a misspelled keyword raises a TypeError.

* feat(wall_x): accept noise in predict_action_chunk

WALL-OSS always drew its own starting noise in the diffusion prediction
path, so a caller could not pass it in. predict_action_chunk and
select_action now take a keyword-only noise argument. select_action passes
it to predict_action_chunk, which forwards it to
Qwen2_5_VLMoEForAction.predict for the diffusion mode. When it is None, the
noise is drawn exactly as before. A given noise is moved to the device and
dtype of the draw it replaces (float32), and the loop does not write into
it, so the caller's tensor is not changed. The fast mode decodes tokens and
does not use it.

* feat(wall_oss_05): accept noise in predict_action_chunk

Wall-OSS-0.5's flow generation already takes a starting sample, but
predict_action_chunk dropped every keyword argument, so a caller's noise
was silently ignored. Take a keyword-only noise, shaped
(batch_size, chunk_size, max_action_dim), like the other flow policies, and
pass it through; select_action passes it on. Without it, the same draw runs
as before. Like EO-1, the methods no longer accept and drop other keywords,
so a misspelled keyword raises a TypeError instead of being ignored.
